title: rec-c2.2-accepted-raw-seam
summary: The accepted-Raw seam. chronos-native persists a Raw record and returns its authoritative EventSeq; services subscribes an observer that derives durable TripwireFired evidence; the live fan-out happens last. dual_push is renamed accept_and_publish (the old name described the dual-write REC-C2 retires) and both spawn and attach go through the same seam. Closes FIND-C2.1-03 with a productive UAT: a real probe produces a real firing that survives restart with the same firing_seq/source_seq.

notes: FIND-C2.2-02: FunctionName tripwire matching diverges between the raw matcher (TripwireCondition::matches(&TraceEvent), which requires TraceEvent.location.function) and the retired live semantic matcher (matching_semantic, which fell back to SemanticEvent.description). Surfaced by the C2.2.2 switchover: drain now reports the persisted firing count, so a FunctionName pattern can no longer match a ptrace syscall stream that carries no function location (m0_04 used to pass only because of the description fallback). This is a behaviour NARROWING, not a regression: tripwire_list's derived fire_count is durable too, so probe_drain and the tripwire view now agree instead of contradicting each other. m0_04 was rewritten to assert the canonical law (count == persisted evidence, invariant under a later subscription) and the narrowing is documented in the test. Whether FunctionName should also consider syscall names is a matcher-semantics decision that belongs to its own cycle, not to the drain switchover.

FIND-C2.2-03: 'partial' completeness status is now never produced by any reader (canonical_drain or events_read). Kept in the vocabulary deliberately for parity with C1; a future reader that can prove evidence loss inside the examined range is the intended owner.

FIND-C2.2-04: browser sessions have NO ExecutionLog. chronos-browser does not depend on chronos-log and BrowserProbeContext carries no log registry, so browser captures have no durable evidence home; the adapter buffer is bounded and drops the oldest events at capacity. C2.2.4 removed the destructive read and stopped probe_stop from emptying the buffer that browser_probe_drain reads, but 'ExecutionLog owns occurrence' is still not true for browser captures. Needs the browser capture loop to append through an accepted-Raw seam: own cycle.

FIND-C2.2-05: m0_04 was passing VACUOUSLY since C2.2.2. tripwire_create rejects 'SyscallEnter' (valid: 'syscall_enter') and m0_04's error branch returned early, so the test exited before its assertion and reported PASS. Fixed in C2.2.5: valid event type, and expect/assert instead of .ok()/return at every subscription call site (also in probe_drain_canonical.rs). Lesson recorded: a green test that cannot fail is worse than a red one. Also: m0_04's exact firing-count equality across two live reads was not a system property (live page boundary race, measured 98 -> 100); the property moved to UAT-C2-01 (bounded growth) and probe_drain_canonical (no inflation of a persisted range).
UAT-C2-01/02/03 were named in proposal.md/tasks.md but never defined anywhere in the repo. C2.2.5 defines them from the cycle's laws and executes them; the definition is the deliverable.

debt.orchestrator_dissent: The gate attributes the medium finding (BrowserAdapter::take_semantic_events is still a destructive read) as pre_existing, because a destructive browser-local read existed before this cycle. I do not fully agree and record why: the SUBSTANCE pre-exists, but the RELOCATION is introduced here. Before C2.2.4 that destructive read was reachable through the shared ProbeBackend trait; now it is an inherent, browser-local method. The relocation is a real improvement (it is what makes the ratchet's CANONICAL=0 honest rather than cosmetic) and it is also a real change to the public surface of chronos-browser. Recording the disagreement rather than silently adopting the gate's classification.
debt.missing_projection_note: Superseded. When the orchestrator first read the artifacts, debt-report.json existed but the declared debt-report.md projection did not, so a projection was generated from the JSON and its hash recorded. The phase then made a final write that produced its OWN projection, replacing the orchestrator's; both hashes above are from that final write. The JSON remains the authority and no gate decision was altered at any point. Recorded because 'the report I hashed' and 'the report on disk' were briefly different files, and that is worth stating rather than papering over.
